newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Jiang Zemin warns U.S. on Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: China's Jiang Zemin warns U.S. on Taiwan.

text.p: China's President Jiang Zemin on Friday warned the United States against backing rival Taiwan and expressed confidence the island would one day be reunited with the mainland.

"If the Taiwan question is not handled properly, Sino-U.S. relations will experience twists and turns, and it will be difficult to enjoy healthy and stable growth," Jiang told Cable News Network (CNN) in an interview.
Jiang did not elaborate on what he meant by "handled properly", but Sino-U.S. ties plunged after Taiwan's President Lee Teng-hui made a landmark private trip to the United States in June 1995.

Ties were further strained when the United States threw its weight behind Taiwan by sending aircraft carriers to waters near the island in March 1996, when China conducted war games and missiles tests to intimidate the island in the run-up to its presidential elections.
Beijing and Taipei have been rivals since the Communists won the Chinese civil war and drove the defeated Nationalists into exile in Taiwan in 1949.

Jiang, who is also chief of China's ruling Communist Party, urged the United States to handle the Taiwan issue cautiously to "prevent this question from disturbing and affecting the improvement and growth of Sino-U.S. relations".
"The Taiwan question...(is) the most important and sensitive issue in Sino-U.S. relations," he said.
Jiang expressed confidence Taiwan would be reunited with the mainland eventually, although he did not say when.
"I'm fully confident that eventually Taiwan will be reunified with the motherland," Jiang said.
"The Taiwan question is a question left over from the civil war of China."
Taiwan's authorities have said they are committed to reunification but only after China embraces democracy and free-market reforms.
The interview was Jiang's first with the Western media since his mentor, Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, died on February 19 at age 92.
